title: Refusal, Appeal and Withdrawal of a Keyturn Host Protection Plan Claim
content:
A claim under the Keyturn Host Protection Plan is refused where the loss falls outside the plan's cover, where the evidence never reached the plan's minimum, where the trip the loss is attributed to did not run, or where the damage was already recorded before the trip began, and the ground of refusal is recorded so that the host can answer it.

### Appeals

A refused claim may be appealed inside the plan's appeal window, counted in whole calendar days from the day the refusal is recorded, and each plan allows only its own number of appeals on one claim; an appeal beyond that number is not taken, however new the evidence looks. The day the refusal was recorded is read from that claim's own record, before the appeal is taken, and an appeal brought on the last day of the window is still inside it. An appeal is decided on evidence that existed at the time of the loss, and photographs taken after a repair has begun are not evidence of the state the vehicle came back in.

### Withdrawal

A host may withdraw their own claim at any time before it is paid, and a withdrawn claim is not counted toward the host's accepted claim count for standing purposes; a refused claim is not counted either, since only accepted claims bear on standing.

### What closure releases

Refusal and withdrawal both release any earnings held back against the claim, and the release happens on the day the claim closes rather than at the next statement.

### Finality

A claim closed by refusal or withdrawal cannot be reopened; a host who wants it looked at again files an appeal inside the window or, once the window has run, nothing further can be done under the plan.

### Boundary illustration (hypothetical)

On a plan publishing an appeal window of 30 calendar days and 2 appeals on one claim, a refusal recorded on a given day may be answered on the thirtieth day after it but not on the thirty-first, and a third appeal on that claim is not taken whatever it carries.
